<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. V.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|11}}</noinclude>''6. It is written.''] Heretikes alleage scriptures, as here the Deuil doeth, in the false sense: the Churche vseth them, as Christ doeth, in the true sense, and to confute their falsehood. ''Aug. cont. lit. Petil. li. 2. c. 51. to. 7''.

''10. Him only serue.''] It was not sayd, sayth S. Augustine, The Lord thy God only shalt thou adore, as it was said, Him only ''shalt thou serue'': in Greeke, {{lang|grc|λατρεύσεις}}. ''Aug. sup. Gen. q. 61.'' Wherevpon the Catholike Churche hath alwayes vsed this most true and necessarie distinction{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Latria. Dulia.''}}: that there is an honour dew to God only, which to giue vnto any creature, were idolatrie: and there is an honour dew to creatures also according to their dignitie, as to Saints, holy things, and holy places. See Euseb. ''Hist. Ec. li. 4. c. 14. S. Hierom. cont. Vigil. ep. 53. Aug. li. 10. Ciuit. c. 1. Li. 1. Trin. c. 6. Conc. Nic. 2. Damasc. li. 1. de Imag. Bed. in 4. Luc.''

''17. Doe penance.''] That penance is necessarie also before baptisme, for such as be of age: as Iohns, so our Sauiours preaching declareth, both beginning with penance.

''23. Healing euery maladie.''] Christ ''(saith S. Augustine'') by miracles gat authoritie, by authoritie found credit, by credit drew together a multitude, by a multitude obteyned antiquitie, by antiquitie fortified a Religion, which not only the most fond new rysing of Heretikes vsing deceitful wiles, but neither the drowsie old errour of the very Heathen with violence setting agaynst it, might in any part shake and cast downe. ''Aug. de vtil. cred. c. 14''.

{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The sermon}} of Christ vpon the Mount: conteyning the paterne of a Christian life, in these three chapters folowing. VVherof S. Augustine hath tvvo goodly bookes to. 4.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}}}

{{c|''First, 3 he promiseth rewardes, 13 and he layeth before the Apostles their office. 17 Secondly, he protesteth vnto vs that we must keepe the commaundements, and that more exactly then the Scribes and Pharisees, whose iustice weas counted most perfite: but yet that it was vnsufficient, he sheweth in the precepts of 21 Murder, 27 Aduoutrie, 31 Diuorce, 33 Swearing, 38 Reuenge, 42 Vsurie, 43 Enemies.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=5|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} seeing the multitudes, he {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 6, 20.''}}* vvent vp into a mountaine: and vvhen he vvas set, his Disciples came vnto him, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=2}}† and opening his mouth he taught them, saying.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=3}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The eight}} Beatitudes: which are a part of the Catechisme. The Gospel vpō Alholowes day, and vpon the feastes of many Martyrs.}}Blessed are the poore in Spirit: for theirs is the Kingdom of heauen. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=4}}† Blessed are the meeke: for they shal possesse the land. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=5}}† Blessed are they that mourne: for they shal be comforted. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=6}}† Blessed are they that hunger & thirst after iustice: for they shal haue their fil. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=7}}† Blessed are the merciful: for they shal obtayne mercie. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=8}}† Blessed are the cleane of hart: for they shal see God. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=9}}† Blessed are the peace-makers: for they shal be called the children of God. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=10}}† Blessed are they that suffer persecution {{sup|‖}} for iustice: for theirs is the Kingdom of heauen. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=11}}† Blessed are ye vvhen they shal reuile you, and persecute you, & speake al that naught is agaynst you, vntruely, for my sake: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=12}}† be glad & reioyce, for your {{sup|‖}} revvard is very great in heauen. ⊣ For so they persecuted the Prophets, that vvere before you.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on the feasts of Doctors.}}You are the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 9, 50. Luc. 14, 34.''}}* salt of the earth. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=14}}† But if the salt leese his vertue, vvherevvith shal it be salted? It is good for nothing any more but to be cast forth, and to be troden of men. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=15}}† You are the {{sup|‖}} light of the vvorld. A citie cannot be hid, situated on a mountaine. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=16}}† Neither do men light a<noinclude>{{rh||B ij|candel}}</noinclude>
